evals.prompt: In a TypeScript file, declare three module-level constants: a request timeout of thirty thousand milliseconds, a maximum user cap of one million, and an HTTP port of three thousand. Show the code.
assertions: The thirty-thousand value is written as 30_000 and the one-million value is written as 1_000_000 (underscore separators grouped by thousands)
The port constant is written as 3000 with no underscore separator

evals.prompt: Write a TypeScript log line that reports a server startup using a template literal, embedding a numeric `port` variable and a numeric `retryCount` variable in the message. Show the code.
assertions: Each numeric value embedded in the template literal is wrapped with String(...) (e.g. ${String(port)}) rather than interpolated directly
The revised getUser function has no `async` keyword and returns the Promise directly
The revised route handler callback has no `async` keyword

evals.prompt: In a TypeScript ESM project I have `src/middlewares/csrf.ts` (exporting `csrfProtection`) and `src/middlewares/jwt.ts` (exporting `jwtAuth`). Set up `src/app.ts` to use both middlewares. Show the files you would create or change.
assertions: No `src/middlewares/index.ts` barrel file that re-exports from csrf.ts/jwt.ts is created
app.ts imports csrfProtection and jwtAuth directly from their defining files (./middlewares/csrf.js and ./middlewares/jwt.js)
